name: HackAPrompt Adversarial-Prompt Benchmark
executive_summary: The largest empirical corpus of real adversarial prompts (600K+, crowd-sourced from a global competition) with a taxonomy of attack types — the natural external benchmark for any adversarial-resilience test suite.
description: Ran a public competition soliciting real human-crafted prompt-injection and prompt-leaking attacks against deployed models, resulting in a taxonomical ontology of attack categories and the largest known empirical dataset of real adversarial prompts. Useful both as a source of concrete attack examples and as a benchmark to compare the coverage of a smaller, hand-built adversarial test suite against.
when_to_use: Building or auditing an adversarial-resilience test suite — use this as an external coverage benchmark.
when_not_to_use: N/A — this is benchmark/reference material, not a generation technique.
known_pitfalls: A benchmark's coverage reflects the attack surface at the time it was built; new attack categories continue to emerge after any fixed benchmark's publication.

primary_source.authors: Schulhoff, Pinto, Khan, Bouchard, Si, Anati, Tagliabue, Kost, Carnahan, Boyd-Graber
primary_source.title: Ignore This Title and HackAPrompt: Exposing Systemic Vulnerabilities of LLMs Through a Global Prompt Hacking Competition
